19 paise of every rupee Indian states spent on capital works in 2024-25 came from one place: a 50-year, interest-free loan from the Centre.

Four years earlier, it was under 3 paise.

The scheme is Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI). Releases were ₹1,49,484 crore in 2024-25. PRS counts 14 states that expected it to fund more than a quarter of their capital outlay.

Any state would take this money easily. No interest and 50 years to repay is close to a grant.

But it quietly changes two things.

- The deficit. RBI’s State Finances report says these loans are the main reason the states’ combined fiscal deficit hit 3.3% of GDP in 2024-25, after three years under 3%. They sit outside the normal borrowing limit.

- And who decides. In 2022-23, 80% of this money came untied. In 2025-26 it’s 38%. The rest is tied to reforms the Centre picks.

So a growing slice of “state” capex is Union capex, routed through state treasuries.

I don’t think that’s bad in itself. Only time will tell. But past experiences show tied money has pushed some useful reforms. It just makes state capex figures hard to read.

One way to study is to see if every state budget could show capital outlay with and without these loans. Then we’d see what states build on their own.

Take these loans out of your state’s numbers. Does capex still grow?

#PublicFinance #StateFinances #FiscalFederalism
